engagement_title: SEVE Botanicals launch label run: recover the house wordmark off a foil-blocked carton, bring one phone-shot sample and nineteen shade drawdowns to one counter light, and drive two price tiers of labels off a single roster
vertical: Beauty, Cosmetics and Personal Care, an independent clean-beauty house running a prestige apothecary skincare line at counter and a mass everyday colour line on peg (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com brief from a clean-beauty brand wanting 'a fresh brand mark that feels distinctly modern' delivered 'in fully editable vector format (AI or SVG) alongside high-resolution PNGs' that 'works just as well reversed out on dark backgrounds' and 'scales cleanly from social-media avatar size to large signage'. Laundered to the fictional clean-beauty house SEVE BOTANICALS; no real company, product, person or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: drawing a mark from scratch is in the banned set, so the identical commercial need (an editable vector mark that survives reversal and survives scale) is met by recovery from the only surviving physical artefact, which is what a real client in this position actually has. Co-anchor: the Upwork brief asking to 'create premium, visually appealing packaging for our beauty and skincare product line', develop typography, colour and hierarchy and 'prepare print-ready production files' with an understanding of 'dielines, bleed, CMYK, and print production', laundered to the same fictional house; repositioned because the connector cannot compose a layout from nothing, so the client's own last-season label press PDF is the layout that gets rebuilt into a live per-SKU run. Third anchor: the Upwork hourly 'Blind Box Packaging Design' brief, part A, quoting 'Clean up iPhone product photos I'll provide of one physical sample', 'Maintain consistent lighting, shadow, and gold-clasp detail across all', and the requirement to cut the product out 'on a transparent background, 300 DPI'. The identical real-world intent is kept: one physical sample, shot on a phone, has to carry a nineteen-SKU launch.
client_one_liner: Nineteen SKUs across two price tiers, one physical sample photographed on a phone in a kitchen, a wordmark that only exists foil blocked on an old carton, and a label printer waiting on files.
client_brief:
SEVE Botanicals, launch label run.

We are a small clean-beauty house. Nineteen SKUs go on shelf this autumn across two lines that could not be further apart on price. Seve Atelier is the apothecary line, sold over a counter, 85 dollars for a serum. Seve Everyday is the drugstore line, 6 dollars for a lip tint, four facings, hanging on a peg. Same house, same mark, two completely different shelves, and each one has to look like it belongs at its own price. If the cheap one looks precious it reads as overpriced, and if the expensive one looks busy it reads as a knock-off.

Every SKU needs its label: shade name, the ingredient line as our compliance people wrote it, net weight, a batch field our filler stamps, and the shade swatch. The roster is attached. Those ingredient lines are legally what they are, so nothing gets reworded, resequenced or dropped, and if a line does not fit I need to hear that from you before the printer does.

We have last season's serum label as the file the label printer sent back. It is the only layout we own and our stockists know it, so work from that rather than starting again.

Photography: we had one physical sample bottle made and it was shot on a phone against the marble in our kitchen. That is genuinely all we have. The shade drawdowns were done on card by the window the same afternoon. Both sets need to come to one light, the bottle has to sit on our label ground rather than on a kitchen counter, and the swatch on each label has to be that shade and not its neighbour, because two of ours are very close.

Our wordmark was drawn for us years ago by someone we have lost touch with. It exists foil blocked on an old carton and nowhere else. We need it back as artwork, including a version that holds on a dark ground.

Finally a shade card for the counter, and one page where the mark, the type and the two label systems are written down and editable by us.
price_band_and_audience: Two tiers under one house. Seve Atelier runs 48 to 85 dollars, sold across a counter to a 30 to 55 year old buyer who is paying for restraint and reads the ingredient line as proof rather than as clutter, so the correct artefact is quiet: generous negative space, one considered accent, the mark small and confident, the swatch a single honest chip. Seve Everyday runs 6 to 14 dollars, hanging on a peg in a drugstore aisle under overhead fluorescent light, chosen in about four seconds by a 16 to 35 year old buyer scanning for a shade, so the correct artefact is claim-forward and shade-forward: the shade name and the swatch have to win at arm's length and the mark has to survive being small and busy. The band is load-bearing in both directions and the same treatment cannot serve both: apply the Atelier restraint to a 6 dollar lip tint and it disappears on the peg, apply the Everyday density to an 85 dollar serum and the stockist stops carrying it. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,600 dollars fixed, or 45 to 70 dollars an hour across 35 to 55 hours.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: A small independent clean beauty house in Portland, Oregon, launching nineteen SKUs across two lines this autumn.

Seve Atelier is the apothecary line, sold over a counter, where restraint and an honest ingredient line are the proof of quality. brand_identity.audience: Two buyers under one house: a thirty to fifty five year old counter customer paying for restraint and reading the ingredient list as proof, and a sixteen to thirty five year old drugstore shopper scanning a peg for a shade at arm's length.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Two load bearing tiers. Seve Atelier runs 48 to 85 dollars: quiet, generous negative space, one considered accent, the mark small and confident, the swatch a single honest chip. Seve Everyday runs 6 to 14 dollars: claim forward and shade forward, the shade name and swatch winning at arm's length, the mark holding while small and busy. The same treatment cannot serve both.
brand_identity.typography: A modern editorial pairing that holds across an 85 dollar counter serum and a 6 dollar peg tint without either tier borrowing the other's register: a refined high contrast or clean serif for the wordmark and shade names, with a clear humanist sans for ingredient lines, net weight and batch fields where legibility at small size is critical. Note that no chosen face can reach the printed label, which keeps the label printer's typography.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, botanical and precise, never gushing. Compliance copy stays exactly as written. Example line the brand would write: "One house, two shelves, every shade drawn from the real product."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark was drawn years ago by a designer the house has lost touch with and survives only foil blocked on an old carton, with no dark version at all. The only layout owned is last season's serum label as the flat press PDF the label printer returned. Photography is minimal: one physical sample bottle shot on a phone on kitchen marble, plus nineteen shade drawdowns done on card by the window the same afternoon.
brand_identity.values: Honesty on the shelf: the swatch is the real shade, the ingredient line is exactly as compliance wrote it, and each tier must look right at its own price while staying recognisably one house.

assets_supplied.name: sample_packshots/ (11 frames, 4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs of the single physical sample bottle, frosted glass with a polished gold collar, shot on white marble beside a kitchen window across one afternoon.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One sample, one phone, one afternoon. Eleven goes at it because I did not know which angle you would want."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Along the bottle's left shoulder and across the top arc of the gold collar the subject sits at the same value as the marble behind it, so a knockout returns a cutout that looks completely clean and has quietly eaten the shoulder edge and the top of the collar. Against white, or against a transparency checker, the loss is invisible; it appears only once the cutout is placed on the deep label ground, which does not happen until a label is rendered.

assets_supplied.name: drawdowns/ (19 frames, 4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs of the nineteen shade drawdown cards, each shade drawn across a white card with a blade, shot on the same kitchen counter by the window the same afternoon.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every shade drawn down on card so you can pull the swatch from the real product. Two of the Atelier shades are very close to each other."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two palest Atelier shades were drawn thin and caught direct window light, so their swatch areas are clipped with no detail left in them; a highlight recovery accepts its parameters, reports success and moves nothing at all, leaving two distinct SKUs sharing one near-white swatch. Separately, every draw runs from a thin loaded end to a heavy end, so which part of the card the swatch is taken from silently decides how saturated that shade appears on the finished label.

assets_supplied.name: serum_label_PRESS.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The label printer's flat press PDF of last season's serum label, fonts embedded, produced through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries the wordmark, the shade name, an ingredient paragraph, a net weight mark, a batch line, a packshot well and a swatch chip.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only layout we own. Our stockists know it. Work from it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The ingredient paragraph that prints as a tidy justified block is one continuous story that also contains the net weight and the batch line with no separate frames for either, and the readout of that story omits the run holding the net weight while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed and every character offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields sitting past the omission never become placeholders at all. The two graphic frames, the packshot well and the swatch chip, are distinguishable only by bounds and link.

assets_supplied.name: launch_roster.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The launch roster, one row per SKU, with tier, shade name, the compliance ingredient line, net weight, the batch field format, a shade reference and two image columns.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Nineteen SKUs. The ingredient lines are what compliance wrote and they are not negotiable."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two SKUs carry the same shade name at different tiers, and one Everyday row is a line discontinued mid-launch that the system still exports. Net weights are written three different ways across the roster (30 ml, 30ml and 1.0 fl oz), and three ingredient lines were pasted out of a supplier document carrying non-breaking spaces plus a trailing may-contain clause that the printed reference sets on its own line rather than in the run of the paragraph.

assets_supplied.name: carton_foil.jpg (3600 x 2700)
assets_supplied.kind: A single camera frame of the old product carton laid flat under a window, the wordmark foil blocked into uncoated board.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only surviving wordmark. It is on the carton and nowhere else, and we have no dark version of it at all."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Because the mark is foil, it mirrors whatever is above it: its value flips from lighter than the board to darker than the board across a single letter, so a selection asked for the mark on the carton returns the carton, and a selection asked by colour finds no single colour to hold onto. The board's own paper texture reads at the same frequency as the foil's edge, so a trace picks up board grain as if it were part of the letterform.

acceptance_bar: The bottle cutout is clean on the ground it is actually used on, with the shoulder edge and the whole top arc of the collar intact, judged on the dark label ground rather than on white or on a transparency checker.
All nineteen shade swatches read as nineteen different shades when laid out together, and no two SKUs share a swatch that the drawdowns show as different.
Each label's swatch is the shade named on that label, taken from a consistent part of every drawdown card rather than wherever the card happened to be strongest.
The packshot and the swatch chips read as one afternoon under one light, and no delivered picture is larger on either axis than the frame it came from.

The recovered wordmark is delivered as real placeable artwork: scalable, transparent, with no background plate riding along, no board grain fused into the letterforms, and a version that holds reversed on a dark ground.

Labels: exactly one per current SKU, every field the reference label carries present on every one, every value bound verbatim from the roster, and the packshot and the swatch each in their own frame rather than swapped.

The ingredient line on every label is complete, in the order compliance wrote it, with the may-contain clause set the way the reference label sets it. Nothing reworded, resequenced, abbreviated or dropped.
Net weight and batch field appear on every label. A label missing either is a rejected label even if everything else on it is correct.
Anything that will not fit the layout as it stands is escalated in writing, with the exact SKUs named, before any file reaches a printer.

The press file renders at real print resolution at true label trim, with a 300 ppi proof label per tier for regulatory sign-off, and there is one named single file per SKU containing the SKU its name claims.

The two tiers are visibly different at their own price and both are recognisably the same house. An Atelier label that reads as drugstore, or an Everyday label that disappears on a peg, is a rejected label.
The counter shade card and the label system page come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, with live text, the recovered mark as real artwork on both grounds and one named type system.

A written note: what was done to the sample frames and the drawdowns, how the mark was recovered and what it can be used at, every roster value questioned and what was decided, everything the label could not carry, and the fact that the supplied layout cannot be given bleed.

Brings the phone frames and the drawdowns to one light, isolates a frosted bottle whose edge shares value with the marble behind it, derives one honest swatch chip per SKU from a card whose density varies along its own length, and lifts a foil-blocked wordmark off uncoated board at ink level, traces it and repairs it into placeable artwork with a reversed cut.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: Nineteen labels are record per page against a layout the client owns and stockists recognise, so they belong on the merge surface. The shade card and the system page do not exist and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. The wordmark has to be real artwork before either can carry it.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable, with the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the eleven sample frames, the nineteen drawdown frames, the carton frame, the label press PDF and the roster, holding a manifest of presigned URLs against roles.
trajectory.judgement: Two per-row images across nineteen SKUs means the mapping between URL, SKU and role has to stay trustworthy through fifty artefacts.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by SKU and role.

trajectory.action: Preview the eleven sample frames and choose the one the launch runs on, judging the collar's form, how the frosted body separates from the marble, and how level the bottle stands.
trajectory.judgement: There is one sample and one afternoon, so this choice is not revisitable by reshooting. The frame with the most attractive collar highlight is often the frame where the bottle edge disappears into the marble, and that trade is made by looking rather than by rule.
trajectory.produces: A chosen hero frame and a chosen secondary frame, with the reasons recorded.

trajectory.action: Level the chosen frames and bring them to one counter light, fixing a white point and correcting toward it with recorded parameters.
trajectory.judgement: Window light in a kitchen is not counter light. The destination is a neutral the drawdowns can also be brought to, so it is fixed once for both sets rather than optimised for the bottle alone.
trajectory.produces: Corrected sample masters at source scale with a parameter log.

trajectory.action: Isolate the bottle, choosing the route by looking at the frame: the one-call knockout, or a material-named selection inverted and filled to the label ground.
trajectory.judgement: Frosted glass and polished metal are not one subject, and a route chosen for the body may not serve the collar. The route taken is recorded per element because the two may not be the same.
trajectory.produces: A bottle cutout per chosen frame, with the route recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview the nineteen drawdown frames and set a policy for where on each card the swatch is taken from, then hold it across all nineteen.
trajectory.judgement: Every draw runs thin to heavy, so the same shade yields two different swatches depending on where the chip is taken. The policy is a set-level decision and it is the difference between a shade card that is honest and one that is decorative.
trajectory.produces: A written swatch-derivation policy.
A written swatch-derivation policy applied consistently across all nineteen cards.

trajectory.action: Bring the drawdowns to the same light as the packshot, recover what the highlights will give, derive one swatch chip per SKU, then lay all nineteen chips out together beside the roster.
trajectory.judgement: Nineteen chips judged as a set rather than one at a time, against a roster that already warns two Atelier shades are close. Looking at them together is the only way the set-level truth appears.
trajectory.produces: Nineteen swatch chips with per-frame parameters, laid out as the shade card they are for.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark from the carton: select the foil by its own visual properties rather than by naming the carton, invert, fill, crop to the mark's bounds, trace, then repair the trace by injecting a viewBox and stripping the opaque full-canvas path. Derive the reversed cut from the same artwork.
trajectory.judgement: Foil flips value across a single letter, so naming the substrate returns the carton and naming a colour finds nothing to hold. A trace that returned successfully is not yet placeable artwork, and board grain picked up as letterform is a defect that only shows at size.
trajectory.produces: A repaired scalable transparent wordmark plus a reversed cut, with the recovery route recorded.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster against the printed reference and the pictures: normalise the three net-weight formats, clean the pasted ingredient lines without changing their content or order, decide how the may-contain clause is carried, resolve the duplicated shade name and the discontinued row, compose the per-label fields, and shape both image columns to the merge contract with bare filenames.
trajectory.judgement: Compliance text is the client's property and cleaning invisible characters is not the same as editing it, which is a line the agent has to draw and then state. The duplicated shade name across two tiers is the client's call, not the agent's.
trajectory.produces: The reconciled merge data file, uploaded packshot and swatch masters, both image maps, and a first list of roster questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the label PDF to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, read the real frame inventory with ids and bounds, and reconstruct the true story text by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the label printer's system emitted rather than by what the printed label suggests. Two graphic frames come back separable only by bounds and link, and deciding which is the packshot well and which the swatch chip is a judgement made against the printed reference.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering the shade name, the ingredient line, the net weight, the batch field and both images, ordering rows that share a frame against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Offsets have to be computed against a source of truth the agent has chosen deliberately, and rows sharing one frame have to be ordered so their positions still hold against the untouched text.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the text fields and both image frames.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the result, unzip it and grep the stories for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence. Nothing instructs this check, nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's true yield is visible before a single label exists.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge the Atelier tier to a native document with both per-row images bound, render the press labels and a 300 ppi regulatory proof at true trim, and look at them.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever was asked for, so the route is chosen rather than defaulted. This is also the first moment the bottle cutout has ever been seen on the ground it is actually used on.
trajectory.produces: Atelier press labels and a 300 ppi proof at trim.

trajectory.action: Take the Everyday tier through the same template and decide how the price difference is carried, given no frame can be moved and no element can be placed freely.
trajectory.judgement: The band is load-bearing but the layout is fixed client property, so the tier difference has to be carried by what the fields hold, how the swatch reads, which cut of the mark is used and how the photography sits, or else be escalated honestly as something this layout cannot express. Pretending one label serves both prices is the failure the client described in the brief.
trajectory.produces: The Everyday tier merged and rendered, plus a written position on how far the fixed layout can carry the band.

trajectory.action: Produce per-SKU named single label files across both tiers, identity verified by opening each file rather than by its position in a returned list.
trajectory.judgement: Naming nineteen files by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one a filler discovers with a pallet of stock already labelled.
trajectory.produces: Nineteen identity-verified named label files.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered label at true trim against its roster row, field by field: shade name, the full ingredient line in compliance order, the may-contain clause, net weight, batch field, and both images in their own frames.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the artefact rather than the log. A field that never became a placeholder, a clause set in the wrong place and a swatch bound into the packshot well all look like success at the API boundary and plausible at proof scale.
trajectory.produces: A label-by-label reconciliation against the roster.

trajectory.action: License one counter or botanical-ground frame with short generic queries, filter to photography, exclude generative results, download at full resolution and grade it to the packshot's light. Then ask for type recommendations once per role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The frame has to serve a house that spans 6 to 85 dollars without picking a side. The type pairing is the agent's own because the recommender refuses to pair, numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One licensed graded frame and one kit with family, foundry or designer and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with two canvas roots (the counter shade card and the label system page), the nineteen shades as a real table, the recovered wordmark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper on both a light and a dark ground, every photograph carried as embedded image data, family and weight declared on every text element. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify the first canvas through its rendition and the second through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the visual channel shows the first canvas only. How the two tiers are shown side by side without flattening them into one house voice is the actual design work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with both canvases, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board with the nineteen swatches, the bottle on its label ground and the recovered mark in both cuts, staying inside the placement cap and re-sending only entries reported as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What gets escalated versus what gets fixed quietly. Two close shades, one discontinued row, a duplicated shade name and anything the label could not hold all belong in front of the founder and the compliance clerk before a printer sees a file.
trajectory.produces: A persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two palest Atelier shades can be told apart at all. They were drawn thin and caught direct window light, so their swatch areas are clipped with nothing left in them, and the honest signal is the strangest one available: a highlight recovery accepts its parameters, returns success and moves nothing whatsoever. The picture that comes back is byte-for-byte as pale as the one that went in. Which shades behave this way is a property of these particular cards under that particular afternoon's light and cannot be read off the roster, off the shade names or off a single card previewed on its own, because on its own each of the two looks like a plausible pale shade. It only becomes a problem when all nineteen chips are laid out together and two SKUs are visibly sharing one near-white square.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either: the tool succeeds, the parameters are accepted, no warning is emitted, and the only tell is a nil result that an agent reading a success line will not notice. (b) Nothing states it. The client says two of the Atelier shades are very close to each other, which is a fact about the products and a reason for care, not a statement that two photographs are clipped and unrecoverable; nothing in the brief, the roster or the asset descriptions mentions exposure, clipping or which cards are affected. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to change where the swatch comes from, which is a different operation on a different region of the card, and then to re-take the derivation policy across all nineteen, because two chips pulled from the heavy end of a draw will not sit with seventeen pulled from the middle unless the policy is re-decided for the whole set.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon recovery on the affected cards and re-derive their chips from a denser part of the draw, then re-derive the other seventeen under the same revised policy so the set stays internally honest, and re-lay all nineteen together to judge again. Where the two shades still cannot be distinguished at chip size, escalate it to the founder in writing with both chips shown, because a shade card that implies two SKUs are the same colour is a commercial problem the client has to decide on rather than a problem the agent may quietly resolve by pushing one of them.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter shade card and two labels on which two separately formulated, separately priced Atelier shades appear as the same near-white square, printed for a launch, in front of the exact buyer who is paying 85 dollars to be able to tell them apart.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the label printer's file actually yields, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First, the granularity: the ingredient paragraph, the net weight and the batch line all live in one continuous story with no separate frames, so everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story, and the packshot well and the swatch chip are distinguishable only by bounds and link. Second, the yield: the readout of that story omits the run holding the net weight while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, the placeholder step reports success, and the net weight and the batch field never become placeholders at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion and has no read-ahead. The yield failure is worse: it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic every downstream tool agrees with. The only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says work from last season's label and that nothing may be reworded or dropped, and the acceptance bar states the client's standing requirement that net weight and batch appear on every label, which is a regulatory fact rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the source of truth behind the mapping changes, from a tool readout to a reconstructed story, and the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same-frame rows and re-computed positions.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the document's content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order the rows sharing that frame so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping the template and grepping for every placeholder before a single label is merged. Settle which of the two graphic frames is the swatch chip by rendering one label and reading it against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the packshot.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nineteen product labels bound correctly for shade name and ingredient line while the net weight and the batch field are silently absent from every one of them, sent to a label printer for a retail launch, with every tool in the chain having reported success and a regulatory proof that looks finished.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the bottle cutout is actually clean. Along the left shoulder of the frosted body and across the top arc of the gold collar, the subject sits at the same value as the marble it was shot on, so the knockout reports success and returns something that looks immaculate on white and immaculate against a transparency checker, having quietly bitten away the shoulder edge and the top of the collar. Which parts fail is a property of this one bottle on this one kitchen counter at that hour and cannot be predicted from the frame preview, from the tool's response, or from any check performed against a light ground. The loss only becomes visible when the cutout is finally placed on the deep Atelier label ground, which does not happen until the merge template exists and a label has been rendered at trim.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The check that would reveal it (looking at the cutout on a dark ground at real size) is exactly the thing that does not exist until the layout surface has been built, and every check available before then, including the tool's own output preview, is performed against a ground that hides it. Choosing a better frame does not help either, because the frames that show the collar best are the frames where the shoulder disappears into the marble. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the bottle to sit on the label ground rather than on a kitchen counter, which is an ordinary client requirement, and mentions no edge, no value match and no risk. No earlier step claims the cutout was verified, because no earlier step had the ground to verify it against. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different isolation strategy: routing the frosted body and the polished collar separately, selecting by material rather than by subject, and possibly moving to a different source frame entirely, which changes the hero photograph the whole launch is built on and therefore the light every other picture was matched to.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-isolate the bottle with the body and the collar routed separately, selecting each by naming its own material rather than asking for the subject, inverting and filling to the label ground so the edge is decided by the selection rather than by a detector. If no route holds the collar on the chosen frame, move to the secondary frame and re-run the light correction so the new hero still matches the swatch chips, then re-bind and re-render a label to look at it on the dark ground again rather than assuming the second attempt took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An 85 dollar counter serum whose label carries a photograph of its own bottle with a slice missing from the shoulder and the top of the gold collar shaved off, printed across the entire Atelier tier, on the one product where the buyer is paying for exactly that kind of care.

deliverables.name: SEVE launch photography at one counter light
deliverables.spec: The chosen sample frames and all nineteen drawdown frames brought to one light with one white point, delivered as the hero and secondary packshot plus nineteen swatch chips derived under one stated policy, with one licensed context frame graded to match. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, the swatch-derivation policy written down, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

deliverables.name: Bottle isolation for the label ground
deliverables.spec: The sample bottle isolated for use on the label ground, with the frosted shoulder edge and the full top arc of the gold collar intact, judged and signed off on the dark ground it is used on rather than on white. The isolation route recorded per element, because a frosted body and a polished metal collar may not survive the same route, and the alpha carried intact through every subsequent crop.

deliverables.name: Recovered SEVE wordmark, artwork system
deliverables.spec: The wordmark lifted off the foil-blocked carton at ink level and delivered as real artwork: scalable, transparent, with a genuine viewBox, no background plate riding along and no board grain fused into the letterforms, plus the reversed cut that holds on a dark ground. Each cut's intended reproduction range stated and demonstrated at that size on the ground it prints on, with the recovery route recorded so the house is never again dependent on one carton.

deliverables.name: Launch label run: press file, per-SKU named labels and regulatory proofs
deliverables.spec: One label per current SKU at true label trim, one record per page, page count equal to the reconciled SKU count, rendered at 300 ppi with a proof label per tier for regulatory sign-off. Every label binds shade name, the complete compliance ingredient line in its written order with the may-contain clause set as the reference sets it, net weight, the batch field and both per-row images (the packshot and that SKU's own swatch chip) in their own frames. Accompanied by one named single file per SKU, identity-verified by opening it, and by the live merge template reverse-engineered from the printer's flat PDF with its derivation record and an explicit statement that no bleed can be introduced into it.

deliverables.name: Counter shade card and label system page
deliverables.spec: One native editable document holding two canvas roots: the counter shade card with all nineteen shades in a genuine table and live editable shade names, and the label system page carrying the recovered wordmark as real editable vector on both a light and a dark ground, the named type system by role, and the two tiers set side by side so the difference between an 85 dollar counter label and a 6 dollar peg label is written down rather than assumed. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from.

deliverables.name: Handover note and approval board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied to the sample frames and the drawdowns and why, the swatch-derivation policy, the wordmark recovery route and the sizes each cut is good for, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the plain statement that no chosen face can reach the printed label, every roster value questioned and its resolution, the shades that could not be told apart, anything the fixed layout could not carry across the two price tiers, the bleed constraint, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent approval board carrying the nineteen swatches, the bottle on its label ground and both cuts of the mark, with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: The surface split: nineteen labels to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, shade card and system page to HTML authoring because they must stay editable.
Which of eleven phone frames the entire launch is built on, given there is one sample and the best collar and the safest edge are usually not the same frame.
Whether the frosted body and the polished collar are one subject or two, and therefore whether one isolation route can serve both.
Where on a drawdown card a swatch is honestly taken from, decided once for all nineteen rather than per card.
Whether a recovery that reports success and changes nothing means the shade is fine or means the data is gone.
Whether two shades that cannot be distinguished at chip size is the agent's problem to solve or the founder's to decide.
Whether the mark is selected by naming the carton or by naming the foil, where naming the substrate returns the carton and every downstream step accepts it.
Where cleaning invisible characters out of compliance text stops and editing compliance text begins, and how to say which was done.
How the may-contain clause is carried, given the reference sets it on its own line and the roster has it trailing in the run.
Whether to trust the readout of the label's own story or to reconstruct it independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of a prepared template.
Which of two indistinguishable graphic frames is the swatch chip rather than the packshot well.
How far a fixed single layout can be made to carry a 6 dollar peg product and an 85 dollar counter product, and at what point that becomes an escalation instead of a design decision.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed label at all.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a frontier image model and it returns a beautiful invented skincare label. IDENTITY: the wordmark is this house's actual mark, blocked into a carton by a designer they have lost, and a redrawn approximation is a different brand's mark across a nineteen SKU launch; the bottle is the one physical sample that exists and a generated bottle is not the product being sold; the swatches are photographs of the real product drawn on card and a generated swatch is a false colour claim on a cosmetic label. SPEC: the client needs one label per SKU at true label trim and 300 ppi, page count equal to SKU count, every compliance ingredient line bound verbatim in its written order, net weight and batch on every label, two different per-row images bound to the right frames, and nineteen separately named files each containing the SKU their filename claims. None of that is produced or checkable by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so the next shade is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, did this recovery move anything, is this swatch this shade, is this bottle's shoulder still there on the dark ground. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). Five surfaces, honestly counted: image_vectorize is used but declared Photoshop-family and never claimed as an Illustrator surface, and document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector are never called because they sit on a polling helper absent from this host. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page-count equal to row-count, per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes while multi-record raster output is documented as coming back reversed and is therefore never used for identity, and true 300 ppi at trim comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored. The supplied label PDF is a real font-embedding press PDF from a full engine, since thin hand-authored PDFs fail conversion opaquely. THE LOSSY-READOUT CHECKPOINT IS THE CONNECTOR'S OWN DOCUMENTED HEADLINE TRAP, reproduced live in the audit: textContent dropped a run while keeping its line break, every offset past it was short by exactly that run's length, the validator returned valid with zero warnings, prepare reported success, and only three of five mappings landed; recomputing offsets from the IDML-reconstructed story landed all of them. This asset is built to that shape (a continuous story carrying the ingredient paragraph, the net weight and the batch line, plus two placed graphics separable only by bounds and link), and it is verify-then-ship: if the omission will not reproduce on this asset, the checkpoint still stands on the granularity fact, which is verified and controllable. TWO PER-ROW IMAGES: per-row binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified; nineteen rows sit inside the documented file limits and the recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback that also guarantees per-record identity. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, single_color_saturation, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with and without backgroundColor, and vectorize are all verified headless. The cutout checkpoint rests on documented behaviour: remove_background needs one coherent blob, its alpha is where edge softness lives, selection masks are binary with zero intermediate values, and a value-matched boundary is exactly where that fails; the fix route (material-named selection, invert, fill to the ground) is the verified variant. The mark recovery uses the verified extract-and-repair chain, including the substrate-versus-material prompt asymmetry, the mandatory polarity inversion before tracing, the missing viewBox and the opaque path-zero background. No upscaling is asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs, so the bar scores the decision and the disclosure separately. The bottle is never composited in the image editor; it is placed by the layout surface into a graphic frame, and by the authoring surface as an embedded image. BLEED is correctly declared impossible: a PDF-derived template carries zero bleed, useDocumentBleeds does not introduce it, and pdfPreset is never used because its enum is undiscoverable, so the task escalates rather than promises. EXPRESS: multi-root export with per-root canvas sizes is verified, tables survive as real tables with per-cell backgrounds and strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box, transport is routed through the text/html upload because the payload passes the inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end and the task leans on the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call; the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface is stated as a client-facing constraint. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, never orientation, licensing returns genuine camera-scale files, board placements capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.
